name: PhantomOS — Event-Sourced Runtime Reconstitution Engine
one_line_value_proposition: A deterministic runtime that rebuilds application state by replaying immutable events, with multi-tenant isolation and a replicated-state reconciler.
buyer_problem: Products that need full auditability and reproducible state often bolt event logs onto mutable databases, leaving two sources of truth that drift.
solution_summary_public: FastAPI + SQLAlchemy backend and React/Vite frontend over a PostgreSQL event store. One reconstructor serves full replay, snapshot creation and incremental replay so they cannot disagree. Multi-worker safety uses Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY and advisory-lock leader election.
differentiators_public: A single apply_event path for replay, snapshots and incremental replay, checked by replay-equivalence tests and by replaycheck in CI.
Cross-tenant write and isolation tests, API-key scope and throttling tests, plugin isolation and sandbox tests.
Replicated-state reconciler limited by policy to a `cluster/` key namespace (never tenant data); off by default.
verified_capabilities: Backend test suite of 19 test modules (isolation, replay equivalence, multi-worker, websockets, money rules, sandbox, key management); GitHub Actions workflow 'phantom-runtime-main' succeeded on main at 9931f6c (merge of PR #53).
Docker Compose deployment (PostgreSQL + backend) and Render blueprint present.
Exact-decimal money arithmetic for DeFi-style event types.
unverified_claims: Backend tests were not run locally in this review (they need PostgreSQL); the CI result is cited instead.
Production use, throughput claims in older reports, and the reconciler transport (none included).
Regulatory status of the finance/DeFi event types.

segments: Platform teams standardizing on event sourcing

public.headline: A stateless runtime where every answer is a replay of an auditable event log.
public.subheadline: PhantomOS stores immutable events in PostgreSQL and reconstructs entity state on demand, with workspaces, API keys, plugin isolation, snapshots and a bounded CRDT reconciler.
public.cost_of_inaction: Drift between event history and current state undermines audit and debugging. Qualitative statement; no statistic is cited.
public_limitations: The reconciler has no transport; it does nothing until authenticated peers are added.
Older report documents in the repository contain performance and completeness claims that were not re-verified here and are not used.
Finance/DeFi features need legal review before any financial-product positioning.
architecture_public: Client → FastAPI routes (events, state, snapshots, workspaces, plugins, v3) → PostgreSQL event store → StateReconstructorV2 (single apply path) → snapshots.
Optional reconciler (CRDT, cluster/ namespace only); LISTEN/NOTIFY event bus; React/Vite dashboard.
public.risk_summary: Financial-regulation exposure of DeFi event types; unverified local test run; reconciler not networked; ownership and AI-authorship review pending; no revenue or customers.

demo.title: Rebuild state from a synthetic event log, then audit determinism
steps: Five synthetic events (init, deposits, a withdrawal, an update) are applied by the production reconstructor.
Each line shows the state after the event, so the replay is visible step by step.
A follow-up replaycheck run over the same events reports PASS.
demo.limitations: Reconstructor only, with synthetic data; the full HTTP service was not started for this demo.
